title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #7

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which living things help waste to decompose? (1 mark)
   A. Fungi and bacteria
   B. Bottles
   C. Plastic bags
   D. Stones

2. What effect is shown when a force starts a still football moving? (1 mark)
   A. Holds it together
   B. Changes shape only
   C. Starts motion
   D. Stops motion

3. Which of these plant parts is usually colourful? (1 mark)
   A. Stem
   B. Flower
   C. Soil
   D. Root

4. A jerrycan holds 20 litres. A leaking tap wastes 40 litres in a day. How many jerrycans is that? (1 mark)
   A. 60
   B. 20
   C. 4
   D. 2

5. Why do we boil water before drinking if it may be unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Heat makes water sweet
   B. Heat makes water heavy
   C. Heat kills germs
   D. Heat removes all salt

6. Which of these passes heat slowly? (1 mark)
   A. Copper
   B. Wood
   C. Aluminium
   D. Iron

7. Why are rotting waste heaps a health danger? (1 mark)
   A. They cool the air
   B. They make water sweet
   C. They attract flies and rats that spread diseases
   D. They make soil red

8. What does mass mean? (1 mark)
   A. How hot an object is
   B. The amount of matter in an object
   C. How bright an object is
   D. The space an object takes up

9. What is the waste passed out by animals called? (1 mark)
   A. Urine and faeces
   B. Milk
   C. Food
   D. Seeds

10. Which of these is heavier: 3 kg of sugar or 3000 g of sugar? (1 mark)
   A. They have the same mass
   B. 3000 g
   C. Cannot tell
   D. 3 kg

11. Which of these is a gas? (1 mark)
   A. Water in a cup
   B. Flour
   C. A wooden spoon
   D. The air in a balloon

12. Which sign of life do ALL living things eventually show? (1 mark)
   A. Flying
   B. Flowering
   C. Making seeds
   D. Dying

13. Which is a correct statement about heat? (1 mark)
   A. It moves from a warm object to a cooler one
   B. It moves from cold to warm
   C. It has mass
   D. It stays still

14. Which of these can change the shape of dough? (1 mark)
   A. Talking to it
   B. Leaving it alone
   C. Looking at it
   D. Pressing with a force

15. Why is burning plastic bad? (1 mark)
   A. It is safe for everyone
   B. It makes good manure
   C. It makes harmful smoke
   D. It makes rain

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. A pupil wants to find out which material is transparent, translucent or opaque. Describe a test. (4 marks)

17. Explain why a football is described as a container of matter although it looks empty. (3 marks)

18. Explain the difference between reducing and reusing water. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

19. Give three safety rules when using sources of light. (3 marks)

20. A tap leaks 4 litres every hour. How much water is lost in 6 hours? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Fungi and bacteria
   Decomposers such as fungi and bacteria break down waste.

2. C — Starts motion
   A push makes a still object move.

3. B — Flower
   Flowers are often brightly coloured.

4. D — 2
   40 divided by 20 = 2.

5. C — Heat kills germs
   Boiling kills many germs.

6. B — Wood
   Wood is a poor passer of heat.

7. C — They attract flies and rats that spread diseases
   Flies and rats carry germs.

8. B — The amount of matter in an object
   Mass is the amount of matter in something.

9. A — Urine and faeces
   Animals remove waste such as urine and faeces.

10. A — They have the same mass
   3 kg equals 3000 g.

11. D — The air in a balloon
   Air is a mixture of gases.

12. D — Dying
   Every living thing dies one day, but not all fly, flower or make seeds.

13. A — It moves from a warm object to a cooler one
   Heat moves from hot to cold.

14. D — Pressing with a force
   A force can squeeze and stretch dough.

15. C — It makes harmful smoke
   Burning plastic gives off harmful smoke.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use a torch in a dark room. Put tissue paper, clear plastic and a book one at a time between the torch and a wall. Record whether all, some or no light passes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for equipment, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for classification.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is full of air. Air is a gas, so it has mass and takes up space. It keeps the ball in shape.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air being matter, 1 mark for it filling the ball.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Reducing means using less water, for example closing the tap. Reusing means using the same water again, for example using washing water for the garden.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for examples.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Never look directly at the sun, do not shine torches in eyes, keep candles and lamps away from curtains and paper, do not touch hot bulbs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: 24 litres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 x 6 and 1 mark for the answer with units.
